subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 24, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 24, 2026

Development continues smoothly across the AcreetionOS codebase with important infrastructure improvements being implemented. We have deployed secret detection configuration in our GitLab CI pipelines to enhance security for all contributors. Additionally, the acreetionos-launcher project now includes a Gradle publish workflow for GitHub Packages, streamlining distribution for our automation tools.

The weekend brought attention to critical kernel updates across multiple streams. Linux kernels 7.1.10 and 6.18.46 have been integrated into our stable repository, addressing the latest LWN security advisories. These updates ensure our users maintain optimal system stability and protection against known vulnerabilities.

We extend our sincere condolences to the open source community following the recent passing of Steve French, longtime Samba contributor and Jeremy Allison colleague. His work on file sharing and network protocols has left an indelible mark on Linux development, and his legacy continues through the projects he helped sustain.

Security remains our top priority and we've compiled the latest updates from major distributions. AlmaLinux has patched ansible-core and pcp, while Debian addressed vulnerabilities in chromium, libgit2, python-httplib2, and sabnzbdplus. Fedora users should update immediately to receive fixes for critical components.

The acreetionos-launcher project has received significant documentation updates with a comprehensive README featuring build badges and an improved feature overview. This makes our Windows migration tool more accessible to new users and provides clearer guidance for developers contributing to the launcher interface.

Community contributions continue to flow in with Natalie's bash2bat conversion script reaching its initial implementation stage. This tool will help users transition bash scripts to batch format, expanding AcreetionOS's cross-platform compatibility. The script framework is now ready for community testing and feedback.

Mirror synchronization completed successfully with updates from August 17, ensuring all distribution channels reflect the latest official packages. Our GitLab instance continues hosting fast, private builds with Cinnamon desktop integration, providing users with multiple download options for their preferred installation method.

The development team continues monitoring CI pipeline performance and has implemented improvements to maintain build reliability. Both Darren and Natalie remain focused on core distribution stability while exploring new automation opportunities for future releases.

Looking ahead, we encourage all users to review the updated kernel packages and launcher documentation. Continue sharing security update requests through our Discord community where Darren and Natalie provide prompt assistance with distribution-specific concerns.
